answer: Across the tundra, a ballot must spin its own thread of time: a chained verifiable delay function, each ballot's input the hash of the last proof from its funding key. Ten thousand cloned ballots die on the chain check: every link needs 12 minutes of serial squaring, even on a $1,000 Chia ASIC, so 10,000 links take 83 days; the epoch closes in 6 hours. Any peer verifies a link in under 10 ms, proof 0.24 KB, and a broken link rejects the ballot and burns its $25 bond. Like a knoll of snow melting one flake at a time, a farm cannot hurry the thaw — its 9,999th ballot is computing at close.
